text: { "entries"  :  [ { "name_han"  :  "太上洞玄靈寶觀妙經"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "The text proves that true insight is not gained by multiplying objects of contemplation, but by a single continuous attention that empties the mind of fixed form; once the observing mind itself is seen as empty, dualistic grasp collapses and the Dao is immediately present. It argues that 'wonder' (妙) is not a special object but the residual clarity left when conceptual seeking stops. Thus cultivation succeeds only when observation turns back upon the observer rather than chasing phenomena."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "1. Premise: ordinary cognition binds itself to names, images, and desired outcomes. 2. Inference: any method that still treats the Dao as an external target reproduces the same binding. 3. Inference: 'viewing wonder' must therefore mean non-grasping awareness of arising and ceasing. 4. Inference: when even the idea of a viewer is released, subject–object polarity loses support. 5. Conclusion: liberation is the spontaneous stillness of empty-yet-aware mind, not acquisition of a mystical vision."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1. In BaZi or life reading, first quiet personal preference before interpreting stems and branches—bias is a form of grasping. 2. Contemplation practice: sit and track breath/thought without labeling outcomes as good or bad. 3. When a chart shows strong 'seeking' patterns (e.g., excessive Fire or agitated Metal), prescribe 'return observation' rather than more action. 4. Use the text as a rule: if a technique increases conceptual complexity without calming the heart-mind, it is counterfeit 'wonder-viewing'. 5. End sessions by releasing the role of 'interpreter' so insight can settle without reification."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike the Huangting corpus, which maps the body as a sacred landscape of deities and organs, this Lingbao scripture abstracts method into pure phenomenology of attention. Unlike Daotong jing’s metaphysical unity thesis, it is operational and anti-reificatory: it proves emptiness of the act of seeing rather than asserting cosmic oneness as doctrine. Its distinctive force is methodological minimalism."  }  ,  { "name_han"  :  "太上洞玄靈寶天尊說大通經"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "The scripture proves that all separate teachings, bodies, and destinies are local expressions of one Great Penetration (大通); fragmentation of practice therefore stems from mistaking provisional names for ultimate division. It argues that when mind recognizes its continuity with the Dao’s unobstructed flow, barriers of self/other and life/death lose ontological weight. Salvation is not relocation to another realm but realization that no genuine blockage ever existed."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "1. Premise: the Dao is characterized as pervasive, unobstructed interconnection. 2. Inference: any real barrier would contradict the Dao’s nature, so barriers must be cognitive. 3. Inference: doctrinal and personal identities arise as temporary naming within that continuum. 4. Inference: clinging to names reifies partial views and produces suffering and sectarian split. 5. Conclusion: 'Great Penetration' is the restoration of unobstructed awareness, after which all methods become transparent means rather than rival truths."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1. In BaZi counseling, treat conflicting chart factors as differentiated expressions of one life-field, not as enemy camps to 'defeat'. 2. When clients feel blocked by fate, reframe blockage as fixation on a partial reading of the whole pattern. 3. Cultivate daily: breathe as if inner and outer qi already communicate without effort. 4. Cross-check multiple systems (BaZi, medical, ethical) as mutually permeable, not hierarchically exclusive. 5. Use '通' as a diagnostic: if a practice isolates the self further, it has failed the Great Penetration test."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Compared with Guanmiao jing’s focus on emptying the act of observation, Daotong jing argues for ontological continuity of all that is observed. Compared with Cantong qi’s laboratory-like correlations of hexagrams, fire phases, and body, this text is more soteriological and less technical: it proves non-obstruction as a metaphysical fact that licenses all skillful means."  }  ,  { "name_han"  :  "上清黄庭养神经"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "The text proves that spirit (神) is not conserved by force or abstraction but by nourishing the living body as the spirit’s dwelling; neglect of form depletes spirit, while regulated breath, organ harmony, and quiet visualization stabilize it. It argues that Shangqing immortality is a hygiene of presence: care for jing–qi–shen in situ rather than flight from the flesh. Longevity and spiritual clarity are two effects of one maintenance system."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "1. Premise: spirit depends on a stable somatic base (organs, breath, fluids). 2. Inference: over-expenditure of attention, desire, and labor wastes the base and scatters spirit. 3. Inference: systematic nourishing practices restore the base and re-gather spirit. 4. Inference: visualization of inner courts reinforces respectful inhabitation of the body-temple. 5. Conclusion: true cultivation is sustained yang-shen—feeding and housing spirit—rather than dramatic supernatural seizure."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1. Map BaZi weakness (e.g., weak Day Master, depleted Water/Metal) to concrete rest, diet, and sleep as spirit-nourishing, not mere lifestyle tips. 2. Daily: short seated regulation of breath before any chart work or ritual. 3. Reduce sensory and emotional leakage that the text treats as spirit-theft. 4. Use gentle organ-focused calm (not violent breath retention) when Fire is excessive in the chart. 5. Teach clients that 'cultivation' includes guarding the vessel that carries destiny’s expression."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike pure Lingbao contemplative emptiness texts, this Shangqing work insists that spirit is cared for through embodied regimen. Unlike later neidan’s abstract lead–mercury algebra, it remains close to medical-hygienic imagery of the Yellow Court. Its proof is: no spirit without maintained dwelling."  }  ,  { "name_han"  :  "上清黄庭五脏六腑真人玉轴经"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "The scripture proves that the five zang and six fu are not only medical organs but seats of true persons (真人) whose order determines both health and spiritual rank; disorder of viscera is disorder of the inner pantheon. It argues that correct visualization, breath, and moral restraint re-enthrone these true persons, thereby aligning microcosm with celestial bureaucracy. Salvation is administrative harmony inside the body-polity."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "1. Premise: each viscus houses a numinous officer or true person. 2. Inference: illness, passion, and dullness are failures of that office’s function. 3. Inference: ritualized awareness of color, position, and spirit of each organ repairs the office. 4. Inference: when all offices report correctly, the whole body becomes a transparent court of the Dao. 5. Conclusion: immortality practice is visceral governance, not abandonment of anatomy."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1. In BaZi, link elemental excess/deficiency to zang-fu hygiene (Wood–Liver, Fire–Heart, etc.) with explicit spirit-governance language. 2. Visualization: daily rotate attention through five zang with their classical colors and calm. 3. Treat anger, anxiety, rumination, grief, and fear as office-level disturbances with organ-specific remedies. 4. Before advanced neidan imagery, establish this visceral map as the operational body. 5. Use '玉轴' idea: keep the axis (central regulation) clear so satellite organs can re-synchronize."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Compared with Huangting yangshen jing’s general nourishing of spirit, this text is more bureaucratic and organ-specific, proving a full inner administration. Compared with medical-only zangfu theory, it sacralizes organs as true persons, so ethics and visualization are as causal as herbs. It is more institutional than the lyrical Inner Landscape poem alone."  }  ,  { "name_han"  :  "黄庭经秘义"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "This esoteric exposition proves that the Yellow Court’s outer verses conceal a single inner law: the middle yellow is the pivot where essence, breath, and spirit are refined into one continuous field. It argues that without grasping that pivot, recitation and imagery remain ornamental; with it, every line becomes an operational key. Secret meaning is structural, not merely cryptic vocabulary."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "1. Premise: surface text uses poetic divine and anatomical images. 2. Inference: those images encode positions and timings of internal work. 3. Inference: the Yellow Court names the central neutral ground that mediates above and below. 4. Inference: secret meaning = how to keep practice at that center so extremes do not leak. 5. Conclusion: esoteric reading is justified only insofar as it restores central, unified operation."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1. When studying Huangting lines, always ask: what does this do to the central pivot (middle dantian / yellow court)? 2. In BaZi terms, privilege chart 'centers' (month command, useful god, balance point) over flashy special stars. 3. Practice: hold soft awareness at the solar plexus / chest-center while breathing, matching 'yellow middle'. 4. Reject secret lore that multiplies gods without returning to one refining process. 5. Use the text to audit other commentaries: if they lose the pivot, they are not truly '秘义'."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike line-by-line scholia that accumulate historical allusions, Miyi claims a structural secret that unifies the poem. Unlike Cantong qi’s hexagram timing, it stays inside Huangting’s body-court symbolism. Its difference is the insistence that secrecy means central method, not social exclusivity."  }  ,  { "name_han"  :  "黄庭内景经秘解"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "The secret explanation of the Inner Landscape proves that 'inner scene' is a workable visionary anatomy: deities, colors, and chambers are instructions for gathering attention inside, not myths to believe from outside. It argues that when the practitioner inhabits this landscape correctly, sensory outflow reverses and spirit consolidates. The text’s authority rests on experiential verifiability of inner loci, not on literary beauty alone."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "1. Premise: consciousness normally leaks through the six senses outward. 2. Inference: naming inner deities and palaces provides addressable points to re-collect attention. 3. Inference: repeated correct dwelling at those points stabilizes jing and qi. 4. Inference: stabilized energy yields clearer spirit and protective integrity. 5. Conclusion: secret interpretation succeeds only when it produces this reversible attention map."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1. Build a personal map of a few reliable inner loci (e.g., upper, middle, lower courts) before expanding the full pantheon. 2. Practice short 'inner tours' after quieting breath—never force visions. 3. In BaZi, treat strong outward Fire/Metal speech patterns as leakage; prescribe inner-scene return. 4. Use secret explanations as checklists for attention placement, not as dogma to recite. 5. Journal somatic markers (warmth, calm, salivation, sleep) as verification of correct reading."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Compared with general Miyi, this work is more systematically Inner Landscape–focused and visionary. Compared with purely philosophical Lingbao texts, it is topographic. It differs from later neidan by retaining Shangqing-style deity architecture rather than replacing it entirely with lead–mercury metaphors."  }  ,  { "name_han"  :  "黄庭内景玉经注解"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "This annotation proves that the Jade Scripture’s verses are mutually defining: each image is glossed by physiological, astronomical, and ethical correlates so the poem becomes a closed instructional system. It argues that without interlinear discipline, readers romanticize the text; with it, the Yellow Court becomes teachable sequence. Commentary is the bridge from lyric to method."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "1. Premise: verse form compresses doctrine and risks ambiguity. 2. Inference: annotation must pin each phrase to body, breath, or moral rule. 3. Inference: cross-references between lines reveal intended order of practice. 4. Inference: where commentary unifies medical and spiritual senses, the text’s dual use is vindicated. 5. Conclusion: reliable cultivation depends on annotated, not free-associative, reading."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1. Study Huangting with a fixed commentary pass: phrase → organ/locus → action → caution. 2. In teaching BaZi students classical texts, model the same: symbol → mechanism → application. 3. Practice only what a line’s annotation can operationalize; table the rest. 4. Compare two annotations on one verse to find the shared operational core. 5. Use annotation discipline to prevent 'vision chasing' without hygiene."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike 'secret solution' texts that claim hidden keys, this genre emphasizes transparent scholastic linkage. Unlike Tongzhu’s pedagogical simplicity, scholarly zhujie often densifies classical allusions. Its distinctive logic is: precision of gloss produces precision of practice."  }  ,  { "name_han"  :  "太上黄庭内景玉经童注"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "The 'child commentary' proves that the Inner Landscape can be made accessible without diluting its soteriological aim: simplified glosses still preserve the claim that inner cultivation is a stepwise, learnable craft. It argues that obscurity is not holiness; if a youth (or beginner) can follow the map, the scripture’s universality is confirmed. Pedagogy itself is a doctrinal proof of the Dao’s approachability."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "1. Premise: the Jade Scripture is often treated as elite and opaque. 2. Inference: if truth is of the Dao, it must admit graded entry. 3. Inference: child-level notes reduce imagery to clear causes and effects. 4. Inference: beginners who stabilize basic breath and reverence validate the text’s practicality. 5. Conclusion: accessibility is not compromise but evidence that the method is real."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1. Teach Huangting in layers: posture and breath → organ calm → inner court names. 2. For BaZi clients new to cultivation, give one image and one daily act, not full pantheons. 3. Use plain language tests: if you cannot explain a line simply, you do not yet own it. 4. Protect beginners from advanced sexual/alchemical readings until basics stabilize. 5. Measure progress by ease and regularity, not by exotic visions."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike dense scholarly annotations and 'secret' commentaries, Tongzhu prioritizes didactic clarity. Unlike Cantong qi commentaries aimed at alchemical adepts, it assumes an early training audience. Its difference is the argument that simplification is fidelity to the text’s life-giving purpose."  }  ,  { "name_han"  :  "黄庭经注"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "A general Huangting commentary proves that Inner and Outer Landscape materials form one hygienic-spiritual continuum: the same body is read as poetic temple and as living organism requiring restraint. It argues that annotation must constantly rejoin beauty of language to regulation of desire, diet, and breath. Without that rejoining, the classic splits into literature versus medicine and loses force."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "1. Premise: Huangting speaks simultaneously in mythic and somatic registers. 2. Inference: commentary that favors only one register falsifies the text. 3. Inference: integrated gloss yields rules for both contemplation and daily conduct. 4. Inference: consistent dual reading produces durable practice communities. 5. Conclusion: the classic’s truth is the unity of aesthetic form and life regimen."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1. When a verse names a deity, also name the organ, emotion, and behavioral restraint it implies. 2. Build a personal 'Huangting rule card': sleep, speech, sexual moderation, breath. 3. In BaZi seasons of stress, return to Outer Landscape-style simple hygiene before Inner Landscape complexity. 4. Use commentary to settle disputes between 'only meditation' and 'only medical' camps. 5. Recite little, embody much: annotation should shrink, not inflate, daily burden."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Compared with specialized 'secret' or 'subtle' commentaries, a standard Huangting zhu is synthetic and balanced. Compared with neidan works that overwrite Huangting with later jindan jargon, it stays closer to the classic’s own dual voice. Its hallmark is integrative moderation."  }  ,  { "name_han"  :  "太上黄庭经发微"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "Fāwēi ('bringing out the subtle') proves that the Yellow Court’s power lies in micro-instructions hidden in ordinary phrases—timings, directions of qi, and faint mental shifts—rather than in spectacular claims. It argues that missing the subtle turns practice coarse, while detecting it allows small correct moves to reorganize the whole field. Subtlety is causal precision, not vagueness."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "1. Premise: coarse practice exhausts and agitates. 2. Inference: the text’s real method must be fine-grained adjustments. 3. Inference: commentary’s task is to extract those micro-operations from poetic diction. 4. Inference: once subtle cues are trained, less force yields more coherence. 5. Conclusion: enlightenment of the text = education of sensitivity."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1. Train discrimination of early signs: mouth dryness, chest tightness, scattered eyes as qi warnings. 2. In BaZi, prefer slight seasonal and elemental rebalancing over dramatic 'cures'. 3. Practice: one subtle breath-lengthening at the first hint of anger or fear. 4. Read each Huangting line asking 'what tiny move does this authorize?' 5. Drop any method that requires strain to feel 'something happening'."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike Tongzhu’s plain pedagogy, Fāwēi assumes the reader can track faint phenomena. Unlike Cantong qi’s macro hexagram clocks, it zooms to micro-phenomenology inside Huangting language. Its difference is equating doctrinal depth with sensory refinement."  }  ,  { "name_han"  :  "黄庭经解"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "A 'jie' (explication) proves that the classic’s meaning is best secured by explanatory paraphrase that reconstructs authorial intent as a coherent teaching program. It argues that solution of difficulties in the text simultaneously solves difficulties in practice: unclear lines mark unclear steps. Understanding is sequential unpacking, not sudden mystical monopoly."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "1. Premise: readers stall where imagery and sequence are obscure. 2. Inference: explication must restore logical order of cultivation stages. 3. Inference: each resolved textual knot corresponds to a practical prerequisite. 4. Inference: a fully explicated text yields a curriculum. 5. Conclusion: '解' is both philological and soteriological clarification."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1. Convert the scripture into a staged syllabus (calm → organ harmony → inner court → non-leakage). 2. When practice fails, locate the earliest unexplained step rather than adding new techniques. 3. For BaZi education, likewise: explain heavenly stems before compound patterns. 4. Write your own short jie of one section monthly to test comprehension. 5. Use explication to refuse random quoting of verses out of order."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Compared with zhujie (interlinear notes) and mi jie (secret keys), jie aims at continuous readable exposition. Compared with neidan 'zhizhi' (direct pointing), it is more discursive. Its identity is curriculum-building through explanation."  }  ,  { "name_han"  :  "黄庭经注解"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "Combined annotation-and-explanation proves that dual apparatus—word-level gloss plus discourse-level interpretation—is necessary to keep the Yellow Court from splitting into either dictionary fragments or free sermon. It argues that only the two together constrain meaning enough for safe embodiment. Scholarly completeness is a safety device for inner work."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "1. Premise: single-mode commentary leaves gaps (terms or arguments). 2. Inference: gaps invite projection and unsafe improvisation. 3. Inference: zhujie + jie covers local and global sense. 4. Inference: constrained meaning yields constrained, testable practice. 5. Conclusion: fullest classical care of the text is ethically part of cultivation."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1. Study method: first gloss hard words, then restate the paragraph’s practice claim. 2. Never visualize a named deity without knowing the glossed organ/function. 3. In BaZi writing, pair technical term definitions with case-level interpretation—the same dual care. 4. Peer-review your reading against another zhujie to catch projection. 5. Treat annotation quality as part of 'guarding the spirit'—sloppy reading is a leak."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "This form differs from pure 'fawei' subtlety hunting by insisting on exhaustive apparatus. It differs from child commentary by retaining scholarly density. Its comparative claim is that methodological completeness prevents spiritual error."  }  ,  { "name_han"  :  "黄庭外景阴符经合注"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "The joint commentary proves that Outer Landscape Huangting and the Yinfu jing share one strategic logic: heaven’s timing and human thrift of energy must coincide, so cultivation is intelligent alignment rather than blind endurance. It argues that outer-scene hygiene (senses, conduct) and Yinfu’s 'thief of opportunity' teaching mutually interpret each other—restraint is tactical, not merely moralistic. Combined reading yields a theory of timely non-waste."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "1. Premise: Outer Huangting regulates the body’s interface with the world. 2. Premise: Yinfu teaches seizing cosmic mechanisms through observation and economy of force. 3. Inference: both target leakage and mistimed action as root failure. 4. Inference: joint annotation reveals shared metrics of timing, thrift, and stillness-in-motion. 5. Conclusion: immortality art is strategic co-agency with natural law, documented across both classics."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1. Pair BaZi timing (luck cycles, annual pillars) with Yinfu-style energy thrift: act when supported, conserve when not. 2. Outer practice: control eyes, speech, and appetite as 'outer landscape' gates. 3. Ask of every effort: is this theft of a natural opening or forced strain? 4. Use joint maxims to design seasonal regimens (spring nurture Wood, autumn gather Metal, etc.). 5. Reject hustle spirituality that ignores mechanism and timing."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike standalone Huangting notes, this text forces cross-classic proof, raising generality. Unlike pure neidan Can Tong commentaries, it stays closer to strategic-natural philosophy of Yinfu plus somatic outer scene. Its difference is the fusion of hygienic exteriority with opportunistic cosmic timing."  }  ,  { "name_han"  :  "参同契阐幽"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "Chanyou ('clarifying the obscure') on the Cantong qi proves that the classic’s dense symbols—hexagrams, planets, furnaces—encode one reversible cycle of advance and withdrawal of fire, not a heap of unrelated secrets. It argues that obscurity dissolves when all images are reduced to phased work on jing–qi–shen under temporal law. Elucidation is unification under process."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "1. Premise: Cantong qi multiplies metaphors that baffle linear reading. 2. Inference: metaphors are parallel languages for one alchemical cycle. 3. Inference: clarifying the obscure means mapping each image onto stage, temperature, and risk. 4. Inference: once mapped, contradictions among images become viewpoint differences, not doctrinal wars. 5. Conclusion: the classic is a single clockwork of refinement disclosed through many masks."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1. Build a phase chart: order, gather, cook, stabilize, withdraw fire—label symbols under these only. 2. In BaZi, analogize luck-cycle 'fire phases': know when to push career Fire and when to withdraw. 3. Practice timed sitting correlated with breath counts or mild daily periods, not random intensity. 4. When two teachers conflict, translate both into phase language before choosing. 5. Safety: any reading that skips 'withdraw fire' is incomplete elucidation."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Compared with Huangting commentaries’ body-palace focus, this work centers temporal alchemy and trigram logic. Compared with Wuzhen pian’s later poetic neidan, it is more Zhouyi-laboratory in flavor. Its signature is systematic de-obscuration by one-cycle reduction."  }  ,  { "name_han"  :  "悟真直指"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "Direct pointing to Awakening to Reality proves that Zhang Boduan’s verses aim at immediate recognition of the true path—humanity’s reverse motion from dissipating life toward the undivided pre-heaven—rather than accumulation of scholastic ornaments. It argues that once the true lead (true intent / true yang) is pointed out, elaborate side doors collapse. Directness is the criterion of orthodoxy."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "1. Premise: many practices claim to be golden elixir yet increase entanglement. 2. Inference: Wuzhen’s standard is return to pre-heaven unity via correct internal medicine. 3. Inference: direct pointing isolates the single pivot (true intention applied to true timing). 4. Inference: side methods fail the test of reversing generative order without residual leakage. 5. Conclusion: awakening is recognition plus correct application of that pivot, not encyclopedic technique."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1. Audit your stack of methods; keep only what clearly serves reverse-refinement, drop the rest. 2. In BaZi counseling, point clients to the useful god (用神) as the chart’s 'true lead'—one pivot, not ten charms. 3. Practice: short sessions of pure intent with breath, avoiding entertainment spirituality. 4. Use '直指' questions: what exactly is being refined, from what, into what? 5. Measure orthodoxy by decreased compulsion and increased stable clarity."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike multi-layered collected commentaries, Zhizhi compresses to the essential needle. Unlike Huangting’s rich inner pantheon, it subordinates imagery to the jindan pivot. It differs from purely philosophical Daoist emptiness texts by insisting on a concrete alchemical reverse path."  }  ,  { "name_han"  :  "周易参同契测疏"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "Ceshu ('investigative subcommentary') proves that the Cantong qi must be tested against the Zhouyi’s structural rules—line positions, nuclear trigrams, waxing–waning—so that alchemical claims remain accountable to the Book of Changes’ logic. It argues that without such measurement, neidan metaphor drifts into free myth; with it, fire phases become rationally schedulable. Yi is the calibration instrument of the Covenant."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "1. Premise: Cantong qi claims identity of Yi, alchemy, and Daoist work. 2. Inference: therefore Yi’s formal constraints must still bind alchemical reading. 3. Inference: subcommentary measures images by hexagram mechanics and cosmology. 4. Inference: readings that violate Yi structure are pseudo-Cantong. 5. Conclusion: true participation in the 'three-in-one' is verifiable by Yi-consistent mapping."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1. When a neidan teacher cites Cantong, ask which hexagram phase and why. 2. Align personal practice intensity with lunar or daily waxing–waning patterns taught via Yi. 3. In BaZi (also a calendrical-stem science), keep the same discipline: symbols must obey generative-control laws. 4. Use investigative notes to slow down and check each analogy. 5. Reject 'anything goes' symbolic inflation."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Compared with Chanyou’s general clarification, Ceshu emphasizes metrological fidelity to Zhouyi. Compared with Wuzhen zhu that may privilege Song neidan experience, this stance is more classicist-Yi. Its difference is making the Changes the court of appeal for alchemical meaning."  }  ,  { "name_han"  :  "周易参同契正义"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "Zhengyi ('correct meaning') proves that among rival Cantong interpretations there is a normative center: moral rectitude, cosmic regularity, and internal refinement must cohere, so 'right meaning' is simultaneously ethical and technical. It argues that deviant readings produce deviant practices—forced, sensual, or purely scholastic. Orthodoxy is the alignment of meaning, motive, and method."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "1. Premise: textual ambiguity spawned competing schools. 2. Inference: a zhengyi must define criteria of correctness beyond taste. 3. Inference: criteria include non-harm, accordance with yin-yang order, and real conservation of essence. 4. Inference: interpretations failing these are not merely different but wrong for cultivation. 5. Conclusion: establishing correct meaning is itself a protective alchemical act."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1. Apply a three-gate test to any method: ethical, cosmological, energetic. 2. In BaZi ethics, refuse fatalism or manipulation that violates rectitude even if 'technically clever'. 3. Prefer gradual, ordered fire to sensational breakthroughs. 4. Keep study notes titled 'what would count as misuse of this line?' 5. Let '正义' humble display—correctness over novelty."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike Maiwang’s possibly more eclectic gathering of insights, Zhengyi is judgmental and standard-setting. Unlike Huangting pedagogical notes, it polices the Cantong tradition’s boundaries. Its distinction is normative adjudication of meaning for the sake of safe elixir work."  }  ,  { "name_han"  :  "参同契脉望"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "Maiwang ('pulse hope' / lineage expectation) proves that the Cantong qi is received as a living artery of transmission: understanding depends on perceiving the pulse of meaning that runs through symbols across generations, not only on isolated philology. It argues that correct hope (望) is oriented expectancy toward the tradition’s vital intent—return to the undivided—while feeling its 'pulse' in practice. Hermeneutics here is medical: take the classic’s pulse."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "1. Premise: a classic survives as lineage, not as a dead inscription. 2. Inference: readers must sense continuity of intent under changing metaphors. 3. Inference: 'pulse' means experiential rhythm matching the text’s advance/withdraw. 4. Inference: hope without pulse is fantasy; pulse without hope is technique without aim. 5. Conclusion: authentic reading joins diagnostic sensitivity with directed aspiration."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1. Read Cantong passages, then sit and sense whether your breath-rhythm matches the described phase. 2. In BaZi, 'take the pulse' of a chart: overall tempo (rushed, stagnant, scattered) before detail. 3. Study under a coherent line of interpretation long enough to feel its pulse; avoid chronic hopping. 4. Keep aspiration (true yang recovery) explicit so technique does not become sport. 5. Use bodily calm and ethical warmth as pulse-signs of right reception."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Compared with Ceshu’s Yi-measurement and Zhengyi’s normative correctness, Maiwang stresses vital, almost clinical reception of tradition. Compared with Wuzhen direct pointing, it is more about sensing continuity than isolating one pivot phrase. Its difference is hermeneia modeled on pulse diagnosis."  }  ,  { "name_han"  :  "悟真篇集注"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "The collected annotations prove that Wuzhen pian’s truth is polyphonic yet convergent: multiple historical notes, when assembled, triangulate a shared neidan grammar of true lead/true mercury, pairing, and timed firing. It argues that no single commentator exhausts the verses, but the ensemble polices extremes and clarifies consensus. Collection is a method of error-correction."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "1. Premise: individual commentaries are partial and historically situated. 2. Inference: gathering them exposes agreements and outliers. 3. Inference: agreements likely mark structural teachings of the root text. 4. Inference: outliers require extra justification or are set aside for practice safety. 5. Conclusion: jizhu produces a probabilistically stronger map of the path of awakening to reality."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1. Study difficult Wuzhen stanzas with at least two annotations side by side. 2. Extract the intersection as your working rule; log divergences as hypotheses, not commands. 3. In BaZi research, likewise collect schools on a pattern, then act from the robust core. 4. Use the collection to dismantle guru-absolutism without falling into relativism. 5. Practice only consensus-safe bases (conserve essence, rectify mind, follow order) while testing disputed refinements cautiously."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike Zhizhi’s single-vector directness, Jizhu is deliberately multi-vocal. Brevity is the stress test of comprehension."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "1. Premise: practitioners drown in expansive alchemical literature. 2. Inference: a short text that still names all necessary factors is a completeness proof by compression. 3. Inference: annotation must keep each phrase strictly operational, resisting re-inflation. 4. Memorize the operational sequence implied by the four hundred words; recite as a checklist before sitting. 2. Translate each technical term into one bodily-mental act you can actually do today. 3. thought: The user wants me to extract logical reasoning from 20 classical Daoist/BaZi related texts and return a structured JSON response. Let me research these texts to provide accurate scholarly analysis rat...

entries.logic_thesis: The text proves that true insight is not gained by multiplying objects of contemplation, but by a single continuous attention that empties the mind of fixed form; once the observing mind itself is seen as empty, dualistic grasp collapses and the Dao is immediately present. It argues that 'wonder' (妙) is not a special object but the residual clarity left when conceptual seeking stops. Thus cultivation succeeds only when observation turns back upon the observer rather than chasing phenomena.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: ordinary cognition binds itself to names, images, and desired outcomes. 2. Inference: any method that still treats the Dao as an external target reproduces the same binding. 3. Inference: 'viewing wonder' must therefore mean non-grasping awareness of arising and ceasing. 4. Inference: when even the idea of a viewer is released, subject–object polarity loses support. 5. Conclusion: liberation is the spontaneous stillness of empty-yet-aware mind, not acquisition of a mystical vision.
entries.logic_practice: 1. In BaZi or life reading, first quiet personal preference before interpreting stems and branches—bias is a form of grasping. 2. Contemplation practice: sit and track breath/thought without labeling outcomes as good or bad. 3. When a chart shows strong 'seeking' patterns (e.g., excessive Fire or agitated Metal), prescribe 'return observation' rather than more action. 4. Use the text as a rule: if a technique increases conceptual complexity without calming the heart-mind, it is counterfeit 'wonder-viewing'. 5. End sessions by releasing the role of 'interpreter' so insight can settle without reification.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike the Huangting corpus, which maps the body as a sacred landscape of deities and organs, this Lingbao scripture abstracts method into pure phenomenology of attention. Unlike Daotong jing’s metaphysical unity thesis, it is operational and anti-reificatory: it proves emptiness of the act of seeing rather than asserting cosmic oneness as doctrine. Its distinctive force is methodological minimalism.

entries.name_han: 太上洞玄靈寶天尊說大通經
entries.logic_thesis: The scripture proves that all separate teachings, bodies, and destinies are local expressions of one Great Penetration (大通); fragmentation of practice therefore stems from mistaking provisional names for ultimate division. It argues that when mind recognizes its continuity with the Dao’s unobstructed flow, barriers of self/other and life/death lose ontological weight. Salvation is not relocation to another realm but realization that no genuine blockage ever existed.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: the Dao is characterized as pervasive, unobstructed interconnection. 2. Inference: any real barrier would contradict the Dao’s nature, so barriers must be cognitive. 3. Inference: doctrinal and personal identities arise as temporary naming within that continuum. 4. Inference: clinging to names reifies partial views and produces suffering and sectarian split. 5. Conclusion: 'Great Penetration' is the restoration of unobstructed awareness, after which all methods become transparent means rather than rival truths.
entries.logic_practice: 1. In BaZi counseling, treat conflicting chart factors as differentiated expressions of one life-field, not as enemy camps to 'defeat'. 2. When clients feel blocked by fate, reframe blockage as fixation on a partial reading of the whole pattern. 3. Cultivate daily: breathe as if inner and outer qi already communicate without effort. 4. Cross-check multiple systems (BaZi, medical, ethical) as mutually permeable, not hierarchically exclusive. 5. Use '通' as a diagnostic: if a practice isolates the self further, it has failed the Great Penetration test.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with Guanmiao jing’s focus on emptying the act of observation, Daotong jing argues for ontological continuity of all that is observed. Compared with Cantong qi’s laboratory-like correlations of hexagrams, fire phases, and body, this text is more soteriological and less technical: it proves non-obstruction as a metaphysical fact that licenses all skillful means.

entries.logic_thesis: The text proves that spirit (神) is not conserved by force or abstraction but by nourishing the living body as the spirit’s dwelling; neglect of form depletes spirit, while regulated breath, organ harmony, and quiet visualization stabilize it. It argues that Shangqing immortality is a hygiene of presence: care for jing–qi–shen in situ rather than flight from the flesh. Longevity and spiritual clarity are two effects of one maintenance system.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: spirit depends on a stable somatic base (organs, breath, fluids). 2. Inference: over-expenditure of attention, desire, and labor wastes the base and scatters spirit. 3. Inference: systematic nourishing practices restore the base and re-gather spirit. 4. Inference: visualization of inner courts reinforces respectful inhabitation of the body-temple. 5. Conclusion: true cultivation is sustained yang-shen—feeding and housing spirit—rather than dramatic supernatural seizure.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Map BaZi weakness (e.g., weak Day Master, depleted Water/Metal) to concrete rest, diet, and sleep as spirit-nourishing, not mere lifestyle tips. 2. Daily: short seated regulation of breath before any chart work or ritual. 3. Reduce sensory and emotional leakage that the text treats as spirit-theft. 4. Use gentle organ-focused calm (not violent breath retention) when Fire is excessive in the chart. 5. Teach clients that 'cultivation' includes guarding the vessel that carries destiny’s expression.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike pure Lingbao contemplative emptiness texts, this Shangqing work insists that spirit is cared for through embodied regimen. Unlike later neidan’s abstract lead–mercury algebra, it remains close to medical-hygienic imagery of the Yellow Court. Its proof is: no spirit without maintained dwelling.

entries.name_han: 上清黄庭五脏六腑真人玉轴经
entries.logic_thesis: The scripture proves that the five zang and six fu are not only medical organs but seats of true persons (真人) whose order determines both health and spiritual rank; disorder of viscera is disorder of the inner pantheon. It argues that correct visualization, breath, and moral restraint re-enthrone these true persons, thereby aligning microcosm with celestial bureaucracy. Salvation is administrative harmony inside the body-polity.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: each viscus houses a numinous officer or true person. 2. Inference: illness, passion, and dullness are failures of that office’s function. 3. Inference: ritualized awareness of color, position, and spirit of each organ repairs the office. 4. Inference: when all offices report correctly, the whole body becomes a transparent court of the Dao. 5. Conclusion: immortality practice is visceral governance, not abandonment of anatomy.
entries.logic_practice: 1. In BaZi, link elemental excess/deficiency to zang-fu hygiene (Wood–Liver, Fire–Heart, etc.) with explicit spirit-governance language. 2. Visualization: daily rotate attention through five zang with their classical colors and calm. 3. Treat anger, anxiety, rumination, grief, and fear as office-level disturbances with organ-specific remedies. 4. Before advanced neidan imagery, establish this visceral map as the operational body. 5. Use '玉轴' idea: keep the axis (central regulation) clear so satellite organs can re-synchronize.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with Huangting yangshen jing’s general nourishing of spirit, this text is more bureaucratic and organ-specific, proving a full inner administration. Compared with medical-only zangfu theory, it sacralizes organs as true persons, so ethics and visualization are as causal as herbs. It is more institutional than the lyrical Inner Landscape poem alone.

entries.logic_thesis: This esoteric exposition proves that the Yellow Court’s outer verses conceal a single inner law: the middle yellow is the pivot where essence, breath, and spirit are refined into one continuous field. It argues that without grasping that pivot, recitation and imagery remain ornamental; with it, every line becomes an operational key. Secret meaning is structural, not merely cryptic vocabulary.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: surface text uses poetic divine and anatomical images. 2. Inference: those images encode positions and timings of internal work. 3. Inference: the Yellow Court names the central neutral ground that mediates above and below. 4. Inference: secret meaning = how to keep practice at that center so extremes do not leak. 5. Conclusion: esoteric reading is justified only insofar as it restores central, unified operation.
entries.logic_practice: 1. When studying Huangting lines, always ask: what does this do to the central pivot (middle dantian / yellow court)? 2. In BaZi terms, privilege chart 'centers' (month command, useful god, balance point) over flashy special stars. 3. Practice: hold soft awareness at the solar plexus / chest-center while breathing, matching 'yellow middle'. 4. Reject secret lore that multiplies gods without returning to one refining process. 5. Use the text to audit other commentaries: if they lose the pivot, they are not truly '秘义'.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike line-by-line scholia that accumulate historical allusions, Miyi claims a structural secret that unifies the poem. Unlike Cantong qi’s hexagram timing, it stays inside Huangting’s body-court symbolism. Its difference is the insistence that secrecy means central method, not social exclusivity.

entries.logic_thesis: The secret explanation of the Inner Landscape proves that 'inner scene' is a workable visionary anatomy: deities, colors, and chambers are instructions for gathering attention inside, not myths to believe from outside. It argues that when the practitioner inhabits this landscape correctly, sensory outflow reverses and spirit consolidates. The text’s authority rests on experiential verifiability of inner loci, not on literary beauty alone.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: consciousness normally leaks through the six senses outward. 2. Inference: naming inner deities and palaces provides addressable points to re-collect attention. 3. Inference: repeated correct dwelling at those points stabilizes jing and qi. 4. Inference: stabilized energy yields clearer spirit and protective integrity. 5. Conclusion: secret interpretation succeeds only when it produces this reversible attention map.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Build a personal map of a few reliable inner loci (e.g., upper, middle, lower courts) before expanding the full pantheon. 2. Practice short 'inner tours' after quieting breath—never force visions. 3. In BaZi, treat strong outward Fire/Metal speech patterns as leakage; prescribe inner-scene return. 4. Use secret explanations as checklists for attention placement, not as dogma to recite. 5. Journal somatic markers (warmth, calm, salivation, sleep) as verification of correct reading.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with general Miyi, this work is more systematically Inner Landscape–focused and visionary. Compared with purely philosophical Lingbao texts, it is topographic. It differs from later neidan by retaining Shangqing-style deity architecture rather than replacing it entirely with lead–mercury metaphors.

entries.logic_thesis: This annotation proves that the Jade Scripture’s verses are mutually defining: each image is glossed by physiological, astronomical, and ethical correlates so the poem becomes a closed instructional system. It argues that without interlinear discipline, readers romanticize the text; with it, the Yellow Court becomes teachable sequence. Commentary is the bridge from lyric to method.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: verse form compresses doctrine and risks ambiguity. 2. Inference: annotation must pin each phrase to body, breath, or moral rule. 3. Inference: cross-references between lines reveal intended order of practice. 4. Inference: where commentary unifies medical and spiritual senses, the text’s dual use is vindicated. 5. Conclusion: reliable cultivation depends on annotated, not free-associative, reading.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Study Huangting with a fixed commentary pass: phrase → organ/locus → action → caution. 2. In teaching BaZi students classical texts, model the same: symbol → mechanism → application. 3. Practice only what a line’s annotation can operationalize; table the rest. 4. Compare two annotations on one verse to find the shared operational core. 5. Use annotation discipline to prevent 'vision chasing' without hygiene.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 'secret solution' texts that claim hidden keys, this genre emphasizes transparent scholastic linkage. Unlike Tongzhu’s pedagogical simplicity, scholarly zhujie often densifies classical allusions. Its distinctive logic is: precision of gloss produces precision of practice.

entries.name_han: 太上黄庭内景玉经童注
entries.logic_thesis: The 'child commentary' proves that the Inner Landscape can be made accessible without diluting its soteriological aim: simplified glosses still preserve the claim that inner cultivation is a stepwise, learnable craft. It argues that obscurity is not holiness; if a youth (or beginner) can follow the map, the scripture’s universality is confirmed. Pedagogy itself is a doctrinal proof of the Dao’s approachability.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: the Jade Scripture is often treated as elite and opaque. 2. Inference: if truth is of the Dao, it must admit graded entry. 3. Inference: child-level notes reduce imagery to clear causes and effects. 4. Inference: beginners who stabilize basic breath and reverence validate the text’s practicality. 5. Conclusion: accessibility is not compromise but evidence that the method is real.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Teach Huangting in layers: posture and breath → organ calm → inner court names. 2. For BaZi clients new to cultivation, give one image and one daily act, not full pantheons. 3. Use plain language tests: if you cannot explain a line simply, you do not yet own it. 4. Protect beginners from advanced sexual/alchemical readings until basics stabilize. 5. Measure progress by ease and regularity, not by exotic visions.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike dense scholarly annotations and 'secret' commentaries, Tongzhu prioritizes didactic clarity. Unlike Cantong qi commentaries aimed at alchemical adepts, it assumes an early training audience. Its difference is the argument that simplification is fidelity to the text’s life-giving purpose.

entries.logic_thesis: A general Huangting commentary proves that Inner and Outer Landscape materials form one hygienic-spiritual continuum: the same body is read as poetic temple and as living organism requiring restraint. It argues that annotation must constantly rejoin beauty of language to regulation of desire, diet, and breath. Without that rejoining, the classic splits into literature versus medicine and loses force.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Huangting speaks simultaneously in mythic and somatic registers. 2. Inference: commentary that favors only one register falsifies the text. 3. Inference: integrated gloss yields rules for both contemplation and daily conduct. 4. Inference: consistent dual reading produces durable practice communities. 5. Conclusion: the classic’s truth is the unity of aesthetic form and life regimen.
entries.logic_practice: 1. When a verse names a deity, also name the organ, emotion, and behavioral restraint it implies. 2. Build a personal 'Huangting rule card': sleep, speech, sexual moderation, breath. 3. In BaZi seasons of stress, return to Outer Landscape-style simple hygiene before Inner Landscape complexity. 4. Use commentary to settle disputes between 'only meditation' and 'only medical' camps. 5. Recite little, embody much: annotation should shrink, not inflate, daily burden.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with specialized 'secret' or 'subtle' commentaries, a standard Huangting zhu is synthetic and balanced. Compared with neidan works that overwrite Huangting with later jindan jargon, it stays closer to the classic’s own dual voice. Its hallmark is integrative moderation.

entries.logic_thesis: Fāwēi ('bringing out the subtle') proves that the Yellow Court’s power lies in micro-instructions hidden in ordinary phrases—timings, directions of qi, and faint mental shifts—rather than in spectacular claims. It argues that missing the subtle turns practice coarse, while detecting it allows small correct moves to reorganize the whole field. Subtlety is causal precision, not vagueness.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: coarse practice exhausts and agitates. 2. Inference: the text’s real method must be fine-grained adjustments. 3. Inference: commentary’s task is to extract those micro-operations from poetic diction. 4. Inference: once subtle cues are trained, less force yields more coherence. 5. Conclusion: enlightenment of the text = education of sensitivity.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Train discrimination of early signs: mouth dryness, chest tightness, scattered eyes as qi warnings. 2. In BaZi, prefer slight seasonal and elemental rebalancing over dramatic 'cures'. 3. Practice: one subtle breath-lengthening at the first hint of anger or fear. 4. Read each Huangting line asking 'what tiny move does this authorize?' 5. Drop any method that requires strain to feel 'something happening'.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Tongzhu’s plain pedagogy, Fāwēi assumes the reader can track faint phenomena. Unlike Cantong qi’s macro hexagram clocks, it zooms to micro-phenomenology inside Huangting language. Its difference is equating doctrinal depth with sensory refinement.

entries.logic_thesis: A 'jie' (explication) proves that the classic’s meaning is best secured by explanatory paraphrase that reconstructs authorial intent as a coherent teaching program. It argues that solution of difficulties in the text simultaneously solves difficulties in practice: unclear lines mark unclear steps. Understanding is sequential unpacking, not sudden mystical monopoly.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: readers stall where imagery and sequence are obscure. 2. Inference: explication must restore logical order of cultivation stages. 3. Inference: each resolved textual knot corresponds to a practical prerequisite. 4. Inference: a fully explicated text yields a curriculum. 5. Conclusion: '解' is both philological and soteriological clarification.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Convert the scripture into a staged syllabus (calm → organ harmony → inner court → non-leakage). 2. When practice fails, locate the earliest unexplained step rather than adding new techniques. 3. For BaZi education, likewise: explain heavenly stems before compound patterns. 4. Write your own short jie of one section monthly to test comprehension. 5. Use explication to refuse random quoting of verses out of order.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with zhujie (interlinear notes) and mi jie (secret keys), jie aims at continuous readable exposition. Compared with neidan 'zhizhi' (direct pointing), it is more discursive. Its identity is curriculum-building through explanation.

entries.logic_thesis: Combined annotation-and-explanation proves that dual apparatus—word-level gloss plus discourse-level interpretation—is necessary to keep the Yellow Court from splitting into either dictionary fragments or free sermon. It argues that only the two together constrain meaning enough for safe embodiment. Scholarly completeness is a safety device for inner work.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: single-mode commentary leaves gaps (terms or arguments). 2. Inference: gaps invite projection and unsafe improvisation. 3. Inference: zhujie + jie covers local and global sense. 4. Inference: constrained meaning yields constrained, testable practice. 5. Conclusion: fullest classical care of the text is ethically part of cultivation.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Study method: first gloss hard words, then restate the paragraph’s practice claim. 2. Never visualize a named deity without knowing the glossed organ/function. 3. In BaZi writing, pair technical term definitions with case-level interpretation—the same dual care. 4. Peer-review your reading against another zhujie to catch projection. 5. Treat annotation quality as part of 'guarding the spirit'—sloppy reading is a leak.
entries.logic_compare: This form differs from pure 'fawei' subtlety hunting by insisting on exhaustive apparatus. It differs from child commentary by retaining scholarly density. Its comparative claim is that methodological completeness prevents spiritual error.

entries.logic_thesis: The joint commentary proves that Outer Landscape Huangting and the Yinfu jing share one strategic logic: heaven’s timing and human thrift of energy must coincide, so cultivation is intelligent alignment rather than blind endurance. It argues that outer-scene hygiene (senses, conduct) and Yinfu’s 'thief of opportunity' teaching mutually interpret each other—restraint is tactical, not merely moralistic. Combined reading yields a theory of timely non-waste.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Outer Huangting regulates the body’s interface with the world. 2. Premise: Yinfu teaches seizing cosmic mechanisms through observation and economy of force. 3. Inference: both target leakage and mistimed action as root failure. 4. Inference: joint annotation reveals shared metrics of timing, thrift, and stillness-in-motion. 5. Conclusion: immortality art is strategic co-agency with natural law, documented across both classics.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Pair BaZi timing (luck cycles, annual pillars) with Yinfu-style energy thrift: act when supported, conserve when not. 2. Outer practice: control eyes, speech, and appetite as 'outer landscape' gates. 3. Ask of every effort: is this theft of a natural opening or forced strain? 4. Use joint maxims to design seasonal regimens (spring nurture Wood, autumn gather Metal, etc.). 5. Reject hustle spirituality that ignores mechanism and timing.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike standalone Huangting notes, this text forces cross-classic proof, raising generality. Unlike pure neidan Can Tong commentaries, it stays closer to strategic-natural philosophy of Yinfu plus somatic outer scene. Its difference is the fusion of hygienic exteriority with opportunistic cosmic timing.

entries.logic_thesis: Chanyou ('clarifying the obscure') on the Cantong qi proves that the classic’s dense symbols—hexagrams, planets, furnaces—encode one reversible cycle of advance and withdrawal of fire, not a heap of unrelated secrets. It argues that obscurity dissolves when all images are reduced to phased work on jing–qi–shen under temporal law. Elucidation is unification under process.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Cantong qi multiplies metaphors that baffle linear reading. 2. Inference: metaphors are parallel languages for one alchemical cycle. 3. Inference: clarifying the obscure means mapping each image onto stage, temperature, and risk. 4. Inference: once mapped, contradictions among images become viewpoint differences, not doctrinal wars. 5. Conclusion: the classic is a single clockwork of refinement disclosed through many masks.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Build a phase chart: order, gather, cook, stabilize, withdraw fire—label symbols under these only. 2. In BaZi, analogize luck-cycle 'fire phases': know when to push career Fire and when to withdraw. 3. Practice timed sitting correlated with breath counts or mild daily periods, not random intensity. 4. When two teachers conflict, translate both into phase language before choosing. 5. Safety: any reading that skips 'withdraw fire' is incomplete elucidation.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with Huangting commentaries’ body-palace focus, this work centers temporal alchemy and trigram logic. Compared with Wuzhen pian’s later poetic neidan, it is more Zhouyi-laboratory in flavor. Its signature is systematic de-obscuration by one-cycle reduction.

entries.logic_thesis: Direct pointing to Awakening to Reality proves that Zhang Boduan’s verses aim at immediate recognition of the true path—humanity’s reverse motion from dissipating life toward the undivided pre-heaven—rather than accumulation of scholastic ornaments. It argues that once the true lead (true intent / true yang) is pointed out, elaborate side doors collapse. Directness is the criterion of orthodoxy.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: many practices claim to be golden elixir yet increase entanglement. 2. Inference: Wuzhen’s standard is return to pre-heaven unity via correct internal medicine. 3. Inference: direct pointing isolates the single pivot (true intention applied to true timing). 4. Inference: side methods fail the test of reversing generative order without residual leakage. 5. Conclusion: awakening is recognition plus correct application of that pivot, not encyclopedic technique.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Audit your stack of methods; keep only what clearly serves reverse-refinement, drop the rest. 2. In BaZi counseling, point clients to the useful god (用神) as the chart’s 'true lead'—one pivot, not ten charms. 3. Practice: short sessions of pure intent with breath, avoiding entertainment spirituality. 4. Use '直指' questions: what exactly is being refined, from what, into what? 5. Measure orthodoxy by decreased compulsion and increased stable clarity.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike multi-layered collected commentaries, Zhizhi compresses to the essential needle. Unlike Huangting’s rich inner pantheon, it subordinates imagery to the jindan pivot. It differs from purely philosophical Daoist emptiness texts by insisting on a concrete alchemical reverse path.

entries.logic_thesis: Ceshu ('investigative subcommentary') proves that the Cantong qi must be tested against the Zhouyi’s structural rules—line positions, nuclear trigrams, waxing–waning—so that alchemical claims remain accountable to the Book of Changes’ logic. It argues that without such measurement, neidan metaphor drifts into free myth; with it, fire phases become rationally schedulable. Yi is the calibration instrument of the Covenant.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Cantong qi claims identity of Yi, alchemy, and Daoist work. 2. Inference: therefore Yi’s formal constraints must still bind alchemical reading. 3. Inference: subcommentary measures images by hexagram mechanics and cosmology. 4. Inference: readings that violate Yi structure are pseudo-Cantong. 5. Conclusion: true participation in the 'three-in-one' is verifiable by Yi-consistent mapping.
entries.logic_practice: 1. When a neidan teacher cites Cantong, ask which hexagram phase and why. 2. Align personal practice intensity with lunar or daily waxing–waning patterns taught via Yi. 3. In BaZi (also a calendrical-stem science), keep the same discipline: symbols must obey generative-control laws. 4. Use investigative notes to slow down and check each analogy. 5. Reject 'anything goes' symbolic inflation.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with Chanyou’s general clarification, Ceshu emphasizes metrological fidelity to Zhouyi. Compared with Wuzhen zhu that may privilege Song neidan experience, this stance is more classicist-Yi. Its difference is making the Changes the court of appeal for alchemical meaning.

entries.logic_thesis: Zhengyi ('correct meaning') proves that among rival Cantong interpretations there is a normative center: moral rectitude, cosmic regularity, and internal refinement must cohere, so 'right meaning' is simultaneously ethical and technical. It argues that deviant readings produce deviant practices—forced, sensual, or purely scholastic. Orthodoxy is the alignment of meaning, motive, and method.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: textual ambiguity spawned competing schools. 2. Inference: a zhengyi must define criteria of correctness beyond taste. 3. Inference: criteria include non-harm, accordance with yin-yang order, and real conservation of essence. 4. Inference: interpretations failing these are not merely different but wrong for cultivation. 5. Conclusion: establishing correct meaning is itself a protective alchemical act.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Apply a three-gate test to any method: ethical, cosmological, energetic. 2. In BaZi ethics, refuse fatalism or manipulation that violates rectitude even if 'technically clever'. 3. Prefer gradual, ordered fire to sensational breakthroughs. 4. Keep study notes titled 'what would count as misuse of this line?' 5. Let '正义' humble display—correctness over novelty.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Maiwang’s possibly more eclectic gathering of insights, Zhengyi is judgmental and standard-setting. Unlike Huangting pedagogical notes, it polices the Cantong tradition’s boundaries. Its distinction is normative adjudication of meaning for the sake of safe elixir work.

entries.logic_thesis: Maiwang ('pulse hope' / lineage expectation) proves that the Cantong qi is received as a living artery of transmission: understanding depends on perceiving the pulse of meaning that runs through symbols across generations, not only on isolated philology. It argues that correct hope (望) is oriented expectancy toward the tradition’s vital intent—return to the undivided—while feeling its 'pulse' in practice. Hermeneutics here is medical: take the classic’s pulse.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: a classic survives as lineage, not as a dead inscription. 2. Inference: readers must sense continuity of intent under changing metaphors. 3. Inference: 'pulse' means experiential rhythm matching the text’s advance/withdraw. 4. Inference: hope without pulse is fantasy; pulse without hope is technique without aim. 5. Conclusion: authentic reading joins diagnostic sensitivity with directed aspiration.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Read Cantong passages, then sit and sense whether your breath-rhythm matches the described phase. 2. In BaZi, 'take the pulse' of a chart: overall tempo (rushed, stagnant, scattered) before detail. 3. Study under a coherent line of interpretation long enough to feel its pulse; avoid chronic hopping. 4. Keep aspiration (true yang recovery) explicit so technique does not become sport. 5. Use bodily calm and ethical warmth as pulse-signs of right reception.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with Ceshu’s Yi-measurement and Zhengyi’s normative correctness, Maiwang stresses vital, almost clinical reception of tradition. Compared with Wuzhen direct pointing, it is more about sensing continuity than isolating one pivot phrase. Its difference is hermeneia modeled on pulse diagnosis.

entries.logic_thesis: The collected annotations prove that Wuzhen pian’s truth is polyphonic yet convergent: multiple historical notes, when assembled, triangulate a shared neidan grammar of true lead/true mercury, pairing, and timed firing. It argues that no single commentator exhausts the verses, but the ensemble polices extremes and clarifies consensus. Collection is a method of error-correction.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: individual commentaries are partial and historically situated. 2. Inference: gathering them exposes agreements and outliers. 3. Inference: agreements likely mark structural teachings of the root text. 4. Inference: outliers require extra justification or are set aside for practice safety. 5. Conclusion: jizhu produces a probabilistically stronger map of the path of awakening to reality.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Study difficult Wuzhen stanzas with at least two annotations side by side. 2. Extract the intersection as your working rule; log divergences as hypotheses, not commands. 3. In BaZi research, likewise collect schools on a pattern, then act from the robust core. 4. Use the collection to dismantle guru-absolutism without falling into relativism. 5. Practice only consensus-safe bases (conserve essence, rectify mind, follow order) while testing disputed refinements cautiously.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Zhizhi’s single-vector directness, Jizhu is deliberately multi-vocal. Unlike one-author Zhengyi, it distributes authority across a corpus of notes. Its comparative strength is critical mass of testimony as a path to orthopraxy.

entries.logic_thesis: Commentary on the Four Hundred Words on the Golden Elixir proves that the entire neidan enterprise can be compressed into a minimal canonical kernel—true earth, true lead, true mercury, firing strength—around which all longer classics orbit. It argues that if the four hundred words are understood operationally, sprawling scriptures become optional expansions; if not, length only multiplies confusion. Brevity is the stress test of comprehension.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: practitioners drown in expansive alchemical literature. 2. Inference: a short text that still names all necessary factors is a completeness proof by compression. 3. Inference: annotation must keep each phrase strictly operational, resisting re-inflation. 4. Inference: successful short-form practice validates the kernel theory of jindan. 5. Conclusion: mastery means being able to return from all books to these few hundred words without remainder.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Memorize the operational sequence implied by the four hundred words; recite as a checklist before sitting. 2. Translate each technical term into one bodily-mental act you can actually do today. 3. In BaZi, learn to state a chart’s remedy in one tight paragraph—the same compression skill. 4. When confused by Huangting or Cantong density, return to this kernel and re-expand only as needed. 5. Quarterly: write your own 400-word (or shorter) synthesis; if you cannot, study is incomplete.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Cantong qi’s archaic multi-system tapestry and Huangting’s visionary anatomy, this text is deliberately minimal and late-neidan in diction. Unlike Wuzhen’s poetic difficulty, it aims at portable doctrine. Its difference is proving completeness through radical compression and commentary that refuses to undo that compression.
